doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Can early jazz be taught?
summary: He compares it to learning a language and credits Wynton Marsalis and Jazz at Lincoln Center for helping credibility.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Is the way those fellows played teachable do you think?

I think so. I think it is. I think it’s like a language, it’s like learning a foreign language. But you have to have a willing student and someone who is not afraid of being criticized about learning that style. And a lot of young people today, you know, they want to be with it, and they want to be where the rest of their musicians are thinking. And if you want to stray a little bit out of that it’s really hard. I can tell youth from that being from my youth. I think it’s a lot possibly easier today. I think what Wynton is doing with his jazz education and his spreading the Gospel, saying that this music is great music, it’s classic music. And it’s part of jazz and it’s all related. And that’s been very helpful. That’s been very helpful. You know you’ve got a major figure, you’ve got a wonderful forum, the Jazz at Lincoln Center, so that gives a lot of credibility to it. You know in my day, it’s a bar here, a gin mill here, you know working for the door and that kind of stuff. And how much can you influence young kids?
